challenge.exploration_summary: context.go defines chi's routing Context which holds URLParams (a RouteParams stack of Keys/Values). It already exposes URLParam(key) for single lookups and has clear, well-tested interfaces (context_test.go). It was a natural place to add convenient bulk accessors over the captured URL parameters.
challenge.feature_spec: Adds three methods to *chi.Context for working with all captured URL parameters: URLParamMap() returns all params as a map[string]string (most-recent value wins on duplicate keys, matching URLParam semantics); URLParamNames() returns the unique parameter names in most-recent-first order; and HasURLParam(key) reports whether a parameter was captured. All three are nil-receiver safe.
challenge.feature_rationale: chi previously only allowed reading URL params one key at a time via URLParam. Middleware, logging, and instrumentation frequently need to enumerate or dump all matched route parameters; these accessors provide that without exposing or duplicating the internal RouteParams stack, following the existing reverse-scan precedence used by URLParam.
challenge.bug_description: URLParamNames() uses an off-by-one loop bound (k > 0 instead of k >= 0) when scanning the captured URLParams stack in reverse. This silently drops the oldest captured parameter (index 0) from the returned name list. When a parameter is only present at index 0 (e.g. a single matched param, or the first-matched param of a multi-param route that is not re-captured later), it is omitted entirely. Callers enumerating route params for logging/instrumentation will miss parameters, leading to incomplete data and incorrect downstream behaviour.

findings.description: Off-by-one error in URLParamNames: the loop condition was `k > 0`, which skips index 0 and therefore never reports the first-captured parameter name. For a context with a single captured param (e.g. only "foo"), URLParamNames() returns an empty slice instead of ["foo"]; more generally the earliest-matched (most ancestral) parameter is always dropped. This yields wrong results consumed by callers iterating over parameter names. Fixed by changing the condition to `k >= 0` so index 0 is included (matching URLParamMap and HasURLParam which correctly use `k >= 0`).

self_review.fix_explanation: Changed the descending loop bound in Context.URLParamNames from `k > 0` to `k >= 0` so the parameter at index 0 (the earliest captured key) is included. The URLParamMap and HasURLParam implementations already used the correct `k >= 0` bound and were left unchanged. All existing and feature tests pass.
